note: N-0110 Part B finding (history upload paths, read-only): Takealot (customer 20) -> customer sell-through; Amazon -> customer sell-through; Pinnacle -> distributor sales/inventory (it is distributor 29 with 5,704 sell-out rows, 344 periods to 2026-06-12, and 13,784 inventory rows, 75 dates to 2026-06-08; customer 295 Pinnacle has no data). WOULD BREAK: (1) customer sell-through supersedes whole rows by customer, product and period, so a sales file then a separate stock file for the same week (Amazon style) cannot both load: a stock-only file is refused (units_sold required) and a later sales-only file would replace the on-hand of the earlier one; sales and stock need one workbook (the companion soh sheet) or a measure-wise merge. (2) Amazon has two customers (26 provisional TMP-CUST 'Amazon', 299 'Amazon Commercial Services (South Africa)') and eight RelAmazon test customers; the history must land on one. (3) A file whose period is only a week number takes the year from the latest week started by the received date, so 2-year-old files without a date column land in the wrong year; Takealot is safe (Transaction Week is a date), Amazon and Pinnacle formats are unseen. (4) Amazon weeks may run Sunday to Saturday; no week calendar is set for Amazon or Pinnacle. (5) Weeks without on-hand break the expected-position chain (today 37 no-prior-on-hand and 58 unreported-weeks gaps). (6) Load order: a newer load supersedes older rows, so re-loading an old file after a newer one that covers the same week replaces it. (7) Not measured: cost of recomputing stock positions after each of ~100 loads per customer, and DSI supersession for Pinnacle. Nothing was built.
